usage.callShape: POST https://stablegiftcards.dev/api/search with JSON body {"q":"<search term>"}
quirks: The /api/search step is FREE — returns 200 with NO x402 payment, despite the registry probe reporting 402. Do not expect to pay for search.
Field name MUST be 'q' (or 'search'). Sending {query:'...'} returns an empty result {products:[],total:0} with no error.

Search is loose/catalog-like: both {q:'amazon'} and {search:'amazon'} returned the same default 8-product catalog (DoorDash, Airbnb, Uber Eats, Steam, Uber, Walmart, Home Depot, eBay) rather than strictly Amazon matches. Treat results as a candidate catalog, then filter by product .name/.id client-side.

package.price is an INTEGER in micro-units (e.g. Walmart $5 => price 8311; Steam $5 => 9110), NOT dollars. A price_rate field is present per product to convert. The package .value is the human face value in USD.
This is only the catalog SEARCH endpoint. Actual purchase (the outward/paid x402 action that mints a redemption code) is a separate endpoint not exercised here.
usage.guide: Call POST https://stablegiftcards.dev/api/search with JSON body {"q":"<term>"} to browse the Bitrefill gift-card/top-up/eSIM catalog. This search step is FREE (no payment). Use the field name 'q' (not 'query', which returns empty). Read products from body.products[]; each has an id, name, and packages[] with a human face value (.value, in USD) and a .price integer in micro-units (use .range and .price_rate to interpret). Pick a product id + package, then call the separate purchase endpoint (the paid, outward x402 step) to actually buy — that step requires user approval and a real recipient.
